question: Should crawl-remote deployments adopt a permanent hidden Gitcrawl canary that survives Worker rollback and fail releases unless both the predecessor and new runtime satisfy the release-bound six-query contract?
rationale: Tests can verify workflow structure, but they cannot choose the long-term stored-data and rollback policy or prove that the cross-repository rollout order and production timing are operationally acceptable.

options.title: Approve after staged proof
options.body: Land the prerequisite contracts first and merge this layer after a staged deployment demonstrates the complete release, propagation, live-coverage, and rollback path.

options.title: Redesign canary lifecycle
options.body: Keep the deployment proof but replace permanent retention with an explicitly migrated or safely garbage-collected canary lifecycle before merge.

options.title: Defer the canary gate
options.body: Pause this layer and continue with the six-query evidence core without making permanent canary validation release-blocking.

recommendation.title: Approve after staged proof
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisite contracts first and merge this layer after a staged deployment demonstrates the complete release, propagation, live-coverage, and rollback path.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current Gitcrawl stack and have the most direct context for coordinating the ClawSweeper and crawl-remote contracts.
